---
title: "beam"
subtitle: "Benchmark Evaluation and Metrics"
---

beam is a metric formalization layer for bioinformatics benchmarks. It ships metric cards (YAML, JSON Schema) with measurement-theory grounded metadata, a multi-criteria decision pipeline with sensitivity primitives, and method-dataset heterogeneity diagnostics.

The metric cards are mapped to STATO, UO, OBI and HuggingFace evaluate where external terms exist; the OWL release artefact at [docs/beam.owl.ttl](docs/beam.owl.ttl) is regenerated from the cards on each release.

## Where to start

- [Quick start](docs/tutorials/quickstart.md). The five-line path from a CSV to an HTML report.
- [How to run from beam.yaml](docs/how-to/run-from-beam-yaml.md). The declarative runner that produces a reproducible artefact.
- [How to use beam from R](docs/how-to/use-beam-from-r.md). The R interface (reticulate-backed; same metric cards and pipeline).
- [Cards and pipeline](docs/explanations/cards-and-pipeline.qmd). What a metric card carries and how the pipeline consumes it.
- [Comparing methods across datasets](docs/explanations/comparing-methods-across-datasets.md). Friedman-Nemenyi and Skillings-Mack.

## Worked vignettes

Each vignette doubles as a CI integration test (rendered on every push):

- [Duo 2018 clustering](examples/duo2018/duo2018.qmd): the canonical walkthrough, 14 methods on 12 single-cell RNA-seq datasets.
- [Simulated scenarios](examples/scenarios/scenarios.qmd): consistency checks against documented ground truth.
- [Transportation modes](examples/transportation/transportation.qmd): cross-domain example with partial coverage.
- [M4 forecasting](examples/m4/m4.qmd): 25 methods on six frequency bands.
- [OpenProblems batch integration](examples/openproblems/openproblems.qmd): MCDA contrasted with the platform's own mean-of-scores rule, plus a Bradley-Terry tree on 50 spatial datasets.
- [Cross-benchmark meta-analysis](examples/cross_benchmark/cross_benchmark.qmd): four single-cell integration benchmarks under one consistent rule.
- [LLM cell type annotation](examples/cell_type_annotation/cell_type_annotation.qmd): GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 against the classical annotators on the Hou and Ji (2024) benchmark, then a cross-benchmark comparison across four LLM annotation benchmarks (GPTCelltype, DeepCellSeek, AnnDictionary, SOAR).
